column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists three thousand sheep before a thousand goats; BSB reverses their order.
The Hebrew repeats “the woman” and “the man” in describing their characters; BSB uses “She” and “her husband.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name before his instructions; BSB combines the instructions with his sending. It describes the greeting as asking about Nabal’s peace or welfare.
The Hebrew repeats “peace” for Nabal, his house, and all he owns; BSB combines these under one “peace.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew calls them “the young men,” where BSB supplies “my young men.” It uses the images of finding favor in the eyes and giving what the hand finds, rendered “find favor with you” and “whatever you can afford” in BSB.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly calls the addressees “David’s servants”; BSB uses “them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes returning and coming with two verbs; BSB combines these as “went back.”
The Hebrew repeats strapping on one’s sword for each man and then David separately. BSB combines David and his men under one action with plural “their swords.”
The Hebrew leaves the young man’s owner unnamed; BSB supplies Nabal. David’s messengers are said to come to “bless” the master, rendered “greet” in BSB.
The Hebrew describes their time together with a verb for walking about; BSB uses “lived among them.”
The Hebrew gives the time pair as “night and day”; BSB has “day and night”.
The Hebrew calls Nabal “a son of worthlessness”; BSB renders the image as “a scoundrel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the woman unnamed and presents David and his men with “behold”; BSB supplies Abigail and says she saw them.
The Hebrew says David “had said,” without a separate reference to just finishing speaking; BSB says he “had just finished saying.”
The Hebrew’s oath names “David’s enemies,” where BSB names David. Its description of the threatened males literally says “one urinating against a wall,” rendered “one of Nabal’s men” in BSB.
The Hebrew names David twice; BSB uses “him” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew asks to speak “in your ears”; BSB leaves the ears image implicit.
The Hebrew asks him not to “set his heart” on Nabal; BSB uses “pay no attention.” It repeats Nabal’s name in the name-and-folly wordplay, where BSB explicitly explains “His name means Fool.”
The Hebrew’s oath refers to “your soul” living; BSB says “you yourself” live. It describes self-help as the hand saving for oneself, rendered “avenging yourself with your own hand” in BSB.
The Hebrew calls the gift “this blessing” and describes the young men walking “at my lord’s feet.” BSB uses “this gift” and those who “follow you.”
The Hebrew promises a “faithful house”; BSB renders this as “a lasting dynasty.”
The Hebrew uses singular “soul of your enemies,” where BSB has plural “lives.” Its sling image explicitly names the sling’s palm or hollow; BSB instead supplies “like stones from a sling.”
Close to the Hebrew.
